newsitem.title: USA: Venezuela Brady debt jumps on rating upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Brady debt jumps on rating upgrade.

text.p: Venezuela's Brady debt rose sharply on the day as its sovereign credit rating was upgraded by a notch, traders said.

Standard & Poor's lifted its rating on the country's long-term foreign currency debt to single B plus from single B and revised the rating outlook to stable from positive. The Brady debt got the B-plus rating.
"It has been rumored all day about a rating change," said a trader, noting that Venezuela Bradys had been well bid through the day way before the rating was announced late afternoon.

But the news surprised some traders, who had attributed the earlier firmness to rumors of Venezuela's impending plan to buyback Brady debt with proceeds from oil field sales. The successful oil contract sales already generated some $1.5 billion on Wednesday.
The progress on the labor reform had also been cited as a factor bolstered investors' confidence, said another trader.
Veneauela FLIRBs VZ6C97=RR rose 1-3/4 to bid 92-1/2, with most of the gains made earlier in the day, he said.
"There were rumors that some proceeds from the oil field sales would be used for Brady buyback," said a trader.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, Luis Raul Matos Azocar, Venezuelan finance miniser, said oil windfall would go into a debt recovery fund and macro-economic stabilization fund.

William Romary, Latin America economic analyst at UBS Securities, who had been cautious about Venezuela's overall economic performance, agreed that the labor reform had so far been very positive, especially with the rejection of indexed wage increase proposal.
The Venezuelan Senate approved the labor law reform on Wednesday and the bill now proceeded to the lower chamber for final approval.
In the broad emerging market, investors were quite upbeat about the general trends, traders said.
"With the sovereign spread at the tightest level this year, things are not cheap," said a trader, "but people are afraid of missing the boat."
The sovereign spread of J.P. Morgan's broad Brady index was 409 basis points as of Wednesday.
If U.S. payroll data for May turned out to be "benign," a strong rally in emerging debt could be expected, he said.

According to a Reuters poll, economists expected that 219,000 new non-farm jobs had been added in May and the unemployment rate at 5.0 percent. The data are scheduled for released at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT on Friday.
Traders noted quite active turnover in Brazil papers after the $3 billion 30-year global bond made to the market on Wednesday.
"We saw a lot of buying Pars and Discounts and selling (Global) 27," noted a trader, adding that hedge funds were the principal players.
Brazil Pars BR4D24=RR rose 3/8 to 66-3/4 bid and Discount BRFLTD24=RR gained 1/2 to 83-3/4 bid. Global 27 BRGLB27=RR nevertheless also added 1/2 to 95-3/4.

Russia dollar Vnesh RUVNUSLNS=RR, which rose to record high at 89 on Wednesday amid optimism over the progress of debt reconciliation, slipped a bit on profit-taking. It was bid 88-1/4, off 1/8 on the day.
